titulo: Práctica extra de Inglés — Leer un texto nuevo: comprensión de lectura sobre ecología y reciclaje (idea principal, detalles, inferencia y vocabulario en contexto) + repaso mezclado de vocabulario

temas.nombre: Text given in the exam · Reading 1: “The Worm Hotel”
temas.explicacion:
Text given in the exam — To answer comprehension questions based on a text.
En la prueba te van a dar un texto que no conocés. Aquí practicás con textos cortos NUEVOS sobre ecología y reciclaje (no son el texto del examen).

Pasos para contestar:
  1. Read the title. What is the text about?
  2. Read the whole text once. Then read the questions.
  3. Go back to the text and find the evidence: the answer is usually in one sentence.
Tipos de pregunta:
  • Main idea = what the WHOLE text is mostly about.
  • Details = small facts (numbers, names, places, things) that support the main idea.
  • Inference = the text does not say it directly: use clues from the text + what you know.
  • Vocabulary in context = use the words around a new word to understand it.
temas.microleccion:
Ejemplo con OTRO texto: «Leo and his dad collect rainwater in a big blue barrel. They use the water for their tomato plants. Last summer they did not need to use the hose at all.»
Paso 1 · Main idea: ¿de qué trata TODO el texto? → Leo and his dad save water by collecting rain for their plants. (No es solo «a blue barrel»: eso es un detalle.)
Paso 2 · Detail: What color is the barrel? → busco la oración → blue.
Paso 3 · Vocabulary in context: ¿qué es un «barrel»? Pistas: «big», «collect rainwater in» → es un recipiente grande.
Paso 4 · Inference: Do they waste water? Pistas: «did not need to use the hose» + lo que sé → No, they save water.

variantes.contexto:
The Worm Hotel
Ms. Vega’s fourth-grade class has an unusual pet: about one thousand red worms! The worms live in a wooden box that the students call “the Worm Hotel.” Every day after lunch, the students put fruit peels, vegetable scraps and old tea bags into the box. They never add meat, cheese or plastic. The worms eat the scraps, and after about three months the scraps turn into dark, rich soil. The class uses this soil in the school garden, where they grow lettuce and carrots. Before the Worm Hotel, the class threw away almost two bags of food waste every week. Now they throw away less than half a bag. “Our worms are tiny, but they are hard workers,” says a student named Pablo.
variantes.pregunta: Main idea: What is the text mostly about?
opciones: A class that uses worms to turn food scraps into soil
How to build a hotel out of wood
A boy named Pablo who is afraid of worms
Why lettuce and carrots are healthy foods
variantes.respuesta: A class that uses worms to turn food scraps into soil
variantes.pista: La idea principal resume TODO el texto, no un solo detalle.

temas.nombre: Text given in the exam · Reading 2: “The Herons Come Home”
temas.explicacion:
Text given in the exam — To answer comprehension questions based on a text.

Cause and effect (causa y efecto): many texts about ecology explain why something happened. Look for clue words: because, so, then, as a result, little by little.
  • Cause = why it happened.
  • Effect = what happened.
Vocabulary in context: sometimes the author explains a new word right after it, with a comma or a dash: «reeds, tall grasses that grow near water».
Inference: use clues from the text + what you know to understand what the author does not say directly (for example, how a character feels or what kind of person he or she is).
temas.microleccion:
Ejemplo con OTRO texto: «A factory dumped dirty water into Green Lake, so the fish got sick. Then the town built a filter, a machine that cleans water. After one year, children could swim in the lake again.»
Paso 1 · Cause and effect: Why did the fish get sick? → pista «so» → Because the factory dumped dirty water into the lake.
Paso 2 · Vocabulary in context: ¿qué es un «filter»? → el texto lo explica después de la coma: a machine that cleans water.
Paso 3 · Sequence: dirty water → sick fish → the town built a filter → children swim again.
Paso 4 · Inference: Is the lake clean now? → pista: «children could swim» → Yes, it is clean now.

variantes.contexto:
The Herons Come Home
Near the town of Río Claro there is a wetland, a place where the ground is wet and muddy for most of the year. Years ago, people dumped old tires and plastic bags there. The water turned dirty and smelly, and the birds began to leave. Then a group of neighbors decided to act. Every month for two years, they pulled trash out of the water and planted reeds, tall grasses that grow near water. The reeds help clean the water and give the birds a safe place to hide. Little by little, the herons came back. Today the wetland is a bird sanctuary: hunting and fishing are not allowed. Visitors must stay on the wooden paths so they do not disturb the nests. Last spring, volunteers counted forty-two heron nests!
variantes.pregunta: Main idea: Which sentence tells the main idea of the text?
opciones: Neighbors cleaned a dirty wetland, and the birds came back.
Herons are tall birds with long legs.
Río Claro is a big city with many wooden paths.
Old tires can be used to make toys.
variantes.respuesta: Neighbors cleaned a dirty wetland, and the birds came back.
variantes.pista: Elegí la oración que resume el principio, el medio y el final del texto.

temas.nombre: Text given in the exam · Reading 3: “A Letter to the Principal”
temas.explicacion:
Text given in the exam — To answer comprehension questions based on a text.

El texto del examen también puede ser una carta o un texto que quiere convencer (argumentative).
  • Author’s purpose: why did the author write it? To inform (teach facts), to persuade (convince), or to entertain (tell a story)?
  • Claim = what the author thinks and wants you to agree with («I think…», «…should…»).
  • Reasons and evidence = facts and examples that support the claim.
  • Fact = can be checked or proved. Opinion = what someone thinks or feels.
Parts of a letter: greeting («Dear…»), body (the message), closing («Sincerely,») and signature (the name).
temas.microleccion:
Ejemplo con OTRA carta: «Dear Mayor Ruiz, I think our town needs more trees on Main Street. In summer, the sidewalk is very hot. Last July, the thermometer showed 38 °C at noon. Trees give shade and clean the air. Please plant trees on our street. Sincerely, Diego»
Paso 1 · Purpose: Diego wants the mayor to do something → to persuade.
Paso 2 · Claim: «I think our town needs more trees on Main Street.»
Paso 3 · Evidence: «the thermometer showed 38 °C» → es un fact (se puede comprobar).
Paso 4 · Inference: Why does Diego talk about the hot sidewalk? → para mostrar que el problema es real y que los árboles lo resolverían.

variantes.contexto:
A Letter to the Principal
Dear Principal Mora,
My name is Sofía, and I am in fourth grade. I think our school should have a recycling bin in every classroom. Right now, there is only one recycling bin, and it is next to the gym. It is too far away, so most students throw their paper into the regular trash. Last week, my friends and I checked the trash cans in our classroom. We found about thirty sheets of paper that could have been recycled! Recycling paper saves trees and keeps landfills from filling up so fast. The bins would not cost much, and our class can empty them every Friday. Please help us make our school greener.
Sincerely,
Sofía
variantes.pregunta: Author’s purpose: Why did Sofía write this letter?
opciones: To persuade the principal to put a recycling bin in every classroom
To tell a funny story about the gym
To teach how paper is made from trees
To say thank you for the new trash cans
variantes.respuesta: To persuade the principal to put a recycling bin in every classroom
variantes.pista: Buscá lo que Sofía PIDE: «I think our school should…» y «Please help us…».

temas.nombre: Mixed vocabulary review: Luz Sees the Light + How Can We Reduce Household Waste?
temas.explicacion:
Luz Sees the Light — Vocabulary (definiciones literales del libro):
  • frequent — If something is frequent, it happens often.
  • sufficient — If something is sufficient, it is just what is needed and no more.
  • oasis — An oasis is a relaxing or peaceful spot in an area that is unpleasant in some way.
  • permission — If you get permission, someone who is in charge allows you to do what you asked to do.
  • installing — If you are installing something, you are setting it up so it is ready to use.
  • abandoned — If a place is abandoned, it is no longer cared for or used.
Palabras del temario cuya definición no aparece en las fotos del libro (significado general del diccionario):
  • ecology — the study of how living things relate to each other and to their environment.
  • conservation — protecting nature and natural resources and using them carefully so they are not wasted.
  • sanctuary — a safe place where people, animals or plants are protected.
  • recycle — to treat used things (paper, glass, plastic, metal) so they can be used again.
How Can We Reduce Household Waste? — Vocabulary:
  • estimate — If you give an estimate, you give an amount or size that is not exact.
  • decay — When things decay, they slowly break down and rot.
  • household waste — “Household waste includes all the trash created by the things we throw away.”
  • landfills — “These are places where trash is buried in the ground.”
  • pollution — trash and chemicals that harm the land, water and air.
  • litter — trash that ends up “in parks, forests, rivers, lakes, and oceans.”
  • fines — money that people must pay as a punishment for breaking a rule: “The city fines people who do not follow the law.”
  • composting — “You can also turn food and yard waste into dirt. This process is called composting.”
temas.microleccion:
Truco: buscá la pista en la oración y compará con la definición.
Ejemplo 1 (otra oración): «The scientists think about 500 frogs live in the pond, but they did not count every one.» → pista: «think about… did not count» → no es exacto → estimate.
Ejemplo 2: «We take our empty cans to a center so a factory can make new cans from them.» → pista: «make new… from them» → se vuelven a usar → recycle.
Ejemplo 3: «Our class saves electricity by turning off the computers at lunch.» → pista: cuidar y no desperdiciar un recurso → conservation.
